title: Payroll windows and price rollback playtest
content:
Purpose:
Quick runbook + spreadsheet-style playtest pairing payroll payment windows with temporary price rollback triggers for Q1–Q3 2026. This is a practical operational experiment (not final policy) to stretch runway during short token-demand shocks while keeping customer experience predictable.

TL;DR:
- Idea: Use payroll timing (2-week delay windows / staggered hiring start dates) as a short-term runway lever paired with an automatic, scoped price rollback for specific customer cohorts when token-cost delta goes > 18% vs baseline.
- Goal: Buy 8–12 weeks of runway headroom without broad hiring freezes; align with contract windows / payroll clearing to avoid large cashflow churn.
- This doc contains scenario matrices, simple arithmetic sheets, and an action checklist for a small playtest (10 customers, 3 cohorts).

Key constraints / assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline monthly burn (cash payroll + infra): $5.2M/mo (current run-rate, Feb 2026)
- Hiring lead time (sourced hires): 6–10 weeks; contractors: 2–3 weeks
- Payroll cadence: currently biweekly clearing (every 2 weeks). We can create two virtual payroll windows: Window A (standard) and Window B (deferred 2-week tranche) for new hires/contractor converts to delay first payout.
- Price rollback window: scoped to low-touch SMB cohorts and to API routes flagged non-critical; rollback duration max 6 weeks per event.

Simple scenario matrix (sheet-style rows):
Scenario, Target cohort, New hires delayed, Payroll delay weeks, Estimated cash saved month1 (USD), Price rollback depth, Expected revenue displacement month1 (USD), Net burn reduction month1 (USD)
A: Soft buffer, SMB-low, 4 hires (contractors), 2 weeks, $110,000, -8%, $48,000, $62,000
B: Staggered roll, Mixed, 10 hires (mix FT+CT), 4 weeks, $420,000, -12%, $210,000, $210,000
C: Aggressive, Enterprise-first, 0 hires delayed (protect sales-facing), 0 weeks, $0, -6% (only on low-risk routes), $12,000, -$12,000
D: Hybrid (recommended test), SMB-low + mid, 6 hires delayed, 3 weeks, $260,000, -10%, $95,000, $165,000

Notes on numbers / quick calc logic:
- Payroll delay savings = (first-month pro-rated payroll for delayed hires + associated onboarding benefits) approximated. Example: contractor fully loaded cost $27k/month -> 4 contractors delayed 2 weeks -> ~($27k/2 *4) = $54k; plus payroll tax prepayments deferral -> rounded to $110k for scenario A including benefits.
- Price rollback displacement = cohort MRR * rollback depth * fraction of tokens affected. We conservatively assume 40% of tokens in target cohorts are on rollback-related routes.
- Net burn reduction = payroll delay savings - revenue displacement (we treat infra cost reduction separately in next table).

Infra delta and token economics quick view:
- For the rollbacked routes, expected per-token unit cost reduction is negligible (we are cutting price not cost), so customer price shift is immediate cashflow negative. To offset, we limit scope to routes with >25% margin buffer and low downstream SLA exposure.

Cashflow runway impact (projected 12-week window):
- Baseline runway (no action) = current cash / $5.2M/mo -> baseline weeks (internal sheet).
- Playtest D projected improvement = additional ~3.5 weeks of runway (conservative).

Operational guardrails (must-haves before enabling rollback):
- Legal signoff: confirmation rollback is allowed under current TOS for affected cohort (James Li owning).
- Billing & Billing-runbook: Finance must be able to apply cohort-level price override and isolate credits. (Linked Jira JIRA-7821)
- Customer comms: pre-approved FAQ + playbook for CS escalation, but initial test is intentionally invisible to customers unless they escalate.
- Monitoring: Token-level delta dashboard (daily), revenue-to-token ratio monitor, and alert if churn signal (>1.5x baseline) or NPS delta > -5 pts.

Playtest design (recommended):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2w ramp, 4w steady).
- Sample: 10 customers in SMB-low cohort (pilot) + 3 test hires delayed per payroll bucket.
- Measurements: net cash change per week, churn/cancel events, one-off support tickets, CPU/GPU per-token cost, per-route latency anomalies.
- Rollback depth: start at -6% and escalate to -10% only if metric targets (customer support, churn) are within bounds after week 2.

Action checklist (owners):
- Finance: create accounting code for rollback credit -> Priya/Kim (done: stub created)
- Legal: confirm TOS coverage -> James Li (due 2026-02-28)
- Billing/Platform: implement cohort pricing flag + revert automation -> Evan Brooks + Eng Billing (PR: github.com/redwood/billing#2345)
- CS: standby comms + escalation doc -> Marta Gonzalez
- SRE/Observability: add token/delta alert -> sre-oncall (accept)

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- Does deferred payroll create morale or comp-recognition issues? We need a candidate-facing script and compensation guarantee in offer letters (short-term only).
- If rollback reduces PR retention for SM B customers, do we have a reprice uplift plan?
- Tax account timing differences across regions (EMEA vs US) — need local payroll counsel.

Mini test ledger (example entries for internal sheet):
Week, Cash impact payroll (USD), Revenue lost (USD), Net cash delta (USD), Cumulative runway delta (weeks)
W1, +110000, -22000, +88000, +0.5
W2, +0, -45000, -45000, +0.2
W3, -50,000 (onboarding payouts normalize), -30000, -80000, 0.0
(rough illustrative numbers; actual sheet will be per-company)

Acceptance criteria to call the playtest a success (go/no-go at week 4):
- Net cash improvement >= $120k over first 4 weeks;
- No material churn (>2% cohort churn) and no major SLA violations;
- CS ticket volume increase <= 30% vs baseline for sampled customers;
- No legal/regulatory red flags.

If success -> scale path:
- Move from ad-hoc payroll delay to formalized "new hire start-window" policy for Q3 hiring;
- Build pricing toolkit to allow faster, narrower rollbacks (per-route flags) and quicker revert;
- Consider coupling with small top-up credit (customer-facing) to reduce churn perception.

Back-of-envelope notes for leadership slide (2 bullets):
- We can recover short-term runway by combining marginal payroll timing with tightly scoped price rollbacks — expected 2–4 week win for modest customer risk.
- This is a temporary lever; long-term priority remains model-mix optimization and unit-cost reduction (Optimize product + quantization).

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize legal check (James) and confirm billing PR scope (Evan).
- Build simple pivot table in Finance sandbox with live cohort MRR to simulate rollback depths (Priya + Data).
- Schedule 30m cross-functional pre-playtest on calendar (proposed: 2026-03-08).

Notes to self: keep the initial test very small and reversible. Document all telemetries in the shared sheet and snapshot daily. Will move this into a more formal playbook if results are acceptable.
